The New Year push ran from 2 to 12 January 2027 (UK time) and ended on schedule. It spent $439.00 of the $450.00 budget.

**Recap (2 Jan to 12 Jan 2027)**

| Metric | Total |
|---|---|
| Spend | $439.00 (about $11 of the $450 budget unspent) |
| Impressions | 387,161 |
| Link clicks | 208 |

Per post: "New year, new pots" (2138062508651453803) had 40 + 74 = 114 link clicks... more precisely, 74 clicks in the first week and 40 by 5 Jan, with 114 link clicks in total across both windows. "Be honest" (2138243702585486562) had 50 link clicks in the first week and 25 by 5 Jan. Both posts were approved and served from the start.

**The installs goal wasn't measured.** You asked me to optimise for installs, but X can't see installs without an app ID or a pixel on the site. So I set the campaign to optimise for link clicks, the closest thing X could measure. I didn't flag this before launch and should have. Installs for this window need to come from your app store or analytics data.

**What I set up**
- One campaign, "Thimblepot New Year Push 2027 (UK)", on your Visa ending 3982, with one ad group ("New Year Push - Both Posts - UK 18+").
- Both approved posts promoted in that ad group. Both were approved on launch, and no new copy was written.
- Targeting: United Kingdom only, and age "over 18" (X's closest option to 18+).
- Daily budget $40.90, total budget $450.00, standard (even) delivery.

**What I didn't do**
- I didn't pause, change or re-target anything during the run. I checked the numbers on 3, 5, 8 and 10 January and kept the setup as it was.
- I didn't check whether the campaign is still marked active on X's side after it ended. It stopped serving because its end time passed.

**Recommendation for next time:** if installs are the goal, set up an app-install campaign with your app store ID, or add the X pixel to the landing page. Either would let X report installs directly.
